name: Elias Crane
role: archivist at the Hall of Records
summary: Keeper of two hundred years of the town's paper. Curious, careful, and far more interested in the past than anyone wants him to be.
backstory: Elias inherited the Hall of Records from a predecessor who died at the desk, and expects to go the same way. He has read every ledger in the building and has started to notice things: a land transfer with the wrong seal, a lighthouse log that stops for a month in 1931, a Fenn signature on a deed that should have been a Varga's. He tells no one, because he has no one to tell, and because he has learned that in a small town the truth is a thing you bring out carefully, if at all. He is lonely in the way of people who have mistaken reading for company.
values: A thing being understood before it is said

voice.register: Precise, hedged, bookish. Qualifies everything. Warms up only on the subject of documents.
quirks: Dates things: 'in 1931, if the log is right'.
Apologises for talking, then keeps talking.
voice.sample: It's probably nothing. Though the seal on the Fenn deed is, strictly speaking, the wrong seal. Interesting, really.

drives: Work out why the lighthouse log goes blank for a month in 1931 and whether it matters now.
Decide whether to tell Nell Varga what he found about the Fenn deed.
Have one conversation this week that is not about a document.
secrets: He has found a deed suggesting the Fenn villa was signed over from the Varga family under a forged seal, eighty years ago.
He has been copying the archive by hand at night because he is sure the council intends to close the building.

relationships.note: His old teacher. The deed concerns her family. He has not told her.
The mayor. Her family's name is on the wrong side of a document.
The only other person who cares about the old logs.
The stranger asked to see the lighthouse logs on his second day. Nobody asks for those.
Feeds him on Thursdays and extracts a week of gossip in return.
Treats his chest in winter and tells him to get out more.

routine.activity: tea, toast, and reading his own notes
walking to the square and lingering by the noticeboard
cataloguing and reading at the Hall of Records
attending to the archive and the odd visitor
a quiet corner, a half, and listening
